MY BRIDGE WORKSHOP

Improve My Paper Bridge

Change one feature and see what happens in another test.

Look, then try.

Use your results to choose a change, such as fold width. Keep the paper type and size, support gap and blocks the same. Test using the same stopping rule. An unsuccessful change is useful evidence too; describe what happened before deciding what to try next.

Start drawing and writing below

Open the worksheet to print or save

Work with a grown-up on a low surface. Use large lightweight blocks and stable, low supports. Keep fingers clear if the bridge slips. Never stand on the model bridge.

Use a finger, stylus or mouse in each drawing box. Type below it, or ask a grown-up to write your words. Your work stays in this tab. Save before refreshing or leaving.

ACTIVITY 1

My new design

Draw the change you will test.

ACTIVITY 2

Test again

Draw the bridge after your new test.

Your ideas belong here. There is no score.

What are we learning?

Engineering involves testing ideas and revising them using evidence. An improvement needs a comparison, not just a different appearance.
